archetypes.name: bash-python-boundary
archetypes.rationale: Plan makes cross-language contract claims (byte-stable SKILL.md literals, test-implement-structure.sh grep assertions, restore-finalize-state.sh preservation) that must align with Python emitted shapes — static panel does not audit this seam.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review whether every claim the plan makes about bash-side structural pins aligns with the Python code it depends on. Focus on: (1) whether the SKILL.md pinned literal tokens the plan says must stay byte-stable are actually what test-implement-structure.sh greps for today; (2) whether restore-finalize-state.sh's proposed preservation branch reads the same key names (STALL_TRACKING, STALL_STEP) that python/finalize.py and python/ship.py write; (3) whether the dual-path read-source split (finalize-state.sh for STALL_TRACKING/STALL_STEP, ship-pr-state.sh for PHASE/RESUME_PHASE/CALLER_KIND/OOS keys) described in the plan's SKILL.md and test-implement-structure.sh sections uses consistent key spellings across both documents. Flag any seam where the plan's prose asserts consistency without citing evidence from both sides of the boundary. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: writer-ordering
archetypes.rationale: Plan introduces a gap-fill writer (_persist_stall_metadata_if_needed) that must not clobber in-loop finalize-state writes; the no-op guard logic and call ordering are complex enough to warrant an independent correctness pass.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the plan's description of _persist_stall_metadata_if_needed and write_finalize_state_merged for ordering correctness. Verify the no-op conditions (STALL_TRACKING=true already present, tmpdir outside allowlist, non-STALLED outcome) cover all paths where run_ship already finalized stall state inline, and identify any STALLED code paths the plan may have missed. Check whether the plan's instruction to prefer ShipResult fields over pre-run ctx for PR_NUMBER/PR_URL/MERGE_RESULT is correctly ordered (ShipResult → existing finalize-state keys → ship-pr-state key-parse) and whether that ordering preserves canonical values set by in-loop writers. Confirm that invoking gap-fill after run_ship returns and before emit_result is safe when the exception handler also converts to STALLED — specifically that the exception-to-ShipResult conversion path always reaches gap-fill with a valid, allowlisted tmpdir. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
